title: Capex absorption: spending ahead of revenue is charged
intuition: Wide rental spreads invite capacity spending; the spending arrives as depreciation before it arrives as revenue, and the market charges the gap in the multiple first and the earnings later.
greatest_assumption: Depreciation and interest land inside the measurement window rather than after the revenue arrives.
observation: Provider capex guides rise while the equity multiple holds and then falls three to six months later.

title: Power chain: the queue decides who earns
intuition: The queue and then the transformer gate energization; while gates bind, installed capacity is scarce and spreads stay wide, which is the provider's window and the equipment maker's pricing power.
greatest_assumption: The queue and equipment gates bind for years rather than clearing through price.
observation: Energized megawatts lag announced megawatts by more than a year across the panel.

title: Equipment scarcity pays the supplier
intuition: Demand pulls on turbines and transformers at once; castings and core steel gate the makers, so lead times extend and the pricing power sits with whoever already has slots and mill capacity.
greatest_assumption: The gates are capacity rather than price, so the margin accrues to incumbents for years.
observation: Lead times and supplier margins rise together across at least two equipment categories.

title: Policy pulls the cycle forward and lengthens the shakeout
intuition: Credits raise after tax returns, capital floods in, capacity overshoots and the adjustment is deeper than it would have been without the subsidy; the analogue is merchant power and telecom fibre.
greatest_assumption: Subsidised capital is less disciplined than equity funded capital.
observation: Capacity announcements accelerate in the quarters after a credit is enacted, and cancellations follow within two years of the first price break.

title: Water and cooling constrain the site and reshape capex
intuition: Water stress turns into rules, rules force closed loop retrofits, and the retrofit spend lands on the provider's capex line, tightening the absorption chain.
greatest_assumption: Water constraints bind locally before they bind globally, so the effect is site by site.
observation: Retrofit announcements cluster in basins under drought measures.

title: Labour is the slowest gate and the fastest cost
intuition: Backlogs pull crews, wage pressure raises installed cost, utilities stretch plans, recovery lags, and the political response shows up as price caps that remove the next cycle's signal.
greatest_assumption: The political channel binds before the capital channel does.
observation: Wage settlements and rate case outcomes move together in the same jurisdictions.

title: Financing flips the sign of the build
intuition: Cheap money funds the marginal builder; expensive money removes the marginal buyer exactly when capacity is arriving, which is how cycles turn without a demand shock.
greatest_assumption: The marginal entrant is funded, not retained earnings funded.
observation: Independent capacity announcements stop within two quarters of a funding shock.

title: Elasticity converts price cuts into volume
intuition: Cheaper inference pulls new workloads; always on agents lift the utilisation floor; the floor is what keeps old silicon economically alive, which is what holds resale values and financing terms.
greatest_assumption: Unused use cases exist below the current price and get adopted within quarters.
observation: Token volume rises in the same quarters that unit prices fall, across two independent price series.

title: Tenant concentration moves the margin from the provider to the buyer
intuition: A few large tenants negotiate hard, spreads compress, revenue per megawatt stalls while capex keeps running, and the funding window depends on the contracts those same tenants sign.
greatest_assumption: The largest tenants have a credible self build threat at all times.
observation: Renewal pricing falls while utilisation stays high, in at least two providers.

title: Where the scarcity margin actually lands
intuition: Scarcity runs from power to equipment to capacity rent; the question the chain asks is who keeps it. Equipment keeps it through lead time pricing, providers keep it only while tenants cannot self build, and the multiple is where the market decides which of the two it believes.
greatest_assumption: The margin is retained by whoever has the least substitutable position.
observation: Supplier gross margins and provider revenue per megawatt move in opposite directions in at least one tight window, and the multiple follows the supplier.

title: Forced flow and the dislocation it leaves
intuition: A leveraged account is forced out, the order consumes displayed depth, the dislocation is measurable, and the reversal is available to whoever is already there without needing to be first.
greatest_assumption: The forced seller is finite, and the reversal is larger than the cost of providing liquidity.
observation: Post event paths reverse inside fifteen minutes more often than random times do, on the recorded tape.
